items.markdown:
UX research tools are `software platforms used to collect user feedback, test prototypes, and analyze behavioral data to guide product design`.[[1]](https://www.qualtrics.com/market-research/ux/)[[2]](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=rDb7VcE_PW0&t=14)

A complete UX research stack is divided into several core categories based on the research workflow:

### 1. Prototype & Usability Testing

These tools let you watch real users interact with designs, wireframes, or live sites to identify friction points.[[1]](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=rDb7VcE_PW0&t=14)[[2]](https://www.qualtrics.com/market-research/ux/)

- Maze : Best for rapid, remote prototype testing with strong integrations into design workflows like Figma.
- UserTesting : Best for video-first, enterprise-grade user testing and stakeholder presentations.
- [UXtweak](https://www.uxtweak.com/) : A versatile platform for mobile app, prototype, and website usability testing.[[1]](https://www.lyssna.com/blog/best-ux-research-tools/)[[2]](https://dovetail.com/ux/ai-tools-for-ux-research/)[[3]](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=rDb7VcE_PW0&t=14)[[4]](https://www.uxtweak.com/)

### 2. Information Architecture & Specialized Testing
Used to optimize site navigation, layouts, and content structure.[[1]](https://www.qualtrics.com/market-research/ux/)

- Optimal Workshop : Specialized in advanced card sorting and tree testing to validate site structures.
- Lyssna : Offers a multi-method suite (card sorting, preference testing, and surveys) with built-in recruitment.[[1]](https://www.lyssna.com/blog/best-ux-research-tools/)

### 3. User Behavior & Analytics
Track quantitative data, clicks, and session flows on live products.[[1]](https://www.lyssna.com/blog/best-ux-research-tools/)[[2]](https://www.qualtrics.com/market-research/ux/)

- Hotjar : Excellent for heatmaps, session recordings, and on-site feedback widgets.
- Loop11 : Focuses on quantitative metrics, task performance, and clickstream data.[[1]](https://www.lyssna.com/blog/best-ux-research-tools/)

### 4. Transcription, Synthesis & Repositories
Centralize customer research, transcribe interviews, and turn qualitative data into searchable insights.[[1]](https://www.userinterviews.com/ux-research-tools-map)[[2]](https://dovetail.com/ux/ai-tools-for-ux-research/)

- Dovetail : A leading customer intelligence hub with AI-powered transcription, tagging, and thematic analysis.
- Notably : Uses AI to help synthesize qualitative research and organize data visually.
- Miro : A visual whiteboard platform widely used for affinity mapping and customer journey workshops.[[1]](https://dovetail.com/ux/ai-tools-for-ux-research/)[[2]](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=NXg7hh7mC-I&t=1)[[3]](https://www.userinterviews.com/ux-research-field-guide-chapter/user-research-tools)

### 5. Recruitment & Participant Management
Handle finding, screening, and incentivizing study participants.[[1]](https://www.userinterviews.com/ux-research-field-guide-chapter/user-research-tools)[[2]](https://www.userinterviews.com/ux-research-tools-map)

- User Interviews : A popular panel and participant recruitment platform.
- Tremendous : Frequently integrated for automated global incentive payouts.[[1]](https://www.tremendous.com/blog/ux-research-tool-roundup/)[[2]](https://www.userinterviews.com/ux-research-field-guide-chapter/user-research-tools)
